title: Trump meets Putin's envoy, says a 'big agreement' on Ukraine is close
dek: After Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House, the President met Kirill Dmitriev and said a deal could 'involve all of Europe'. The Kremlin says Europeans cannot join next week's Abu Dhabi talks.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
President Donald Trump met Vladimir Putin's special envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, at the White House on Thursday and afterwards said he was "very close" to settling the Russia-Ukraine war, in an agreement he said could reach beyond Ukraine. "There's going to be an agreement. It's going to be a big agreement, and it's going to involve more than Ukraine," Trump told reporters, adding that it could involve "all of Europe", according to Australian Associated Press and Al Jazeera. He gave no details of the talks, and said he had not met the Ukrainian delegation.

Dmitriev was in Washington for a meeting hosted earlier on Thursday by First Lady Melania Trump, which brought Russian and Ukrainian officials together at the White House to mark the humanitarian ceasefire she helped broker in the occupied town of Oleshky. The two meetings come four days before US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

## Trump and Dmitriev

Trump has often said a deal was near; the talks have stalled over the Donbas region, where Russia demands all of the territory and Ukraine refuses to give up the part it holds. His remark that a deal could take in "all of Europe" was not explained. The Kremlin has so far rejected a wider format. Its spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said European representatives could not take part in the Abu Dhabi talks because the three-way format had been agreed at the outset, TASS reported.

Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys, said on X that the US would "consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines and, if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation", TASS reported. He said officials meeting in Brussels had held "productive and substantive discussions" on security guarantees for Ukraine, and that any arrangements "must fully respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independent decision-making of every nation", AAP reported. Peskov has said the Abu Dhabi talks will focus on security guarantees and will be held behind closed doors.

Neither the Kremlin nor Kyiv had commented on Trump's remarks by Friday morning.

## The White House meeting

NBC News described Mrs Trump's gathering as the first face-to-face meeting of the two sides at the White House since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. She urged both sides to build something "more enduring than a temporary ceasefire", and handed the two delegations personal letters for President Putin and President Volodymyr Zelensky. Neither the White House nor the recipients have said what the letters contain.

Russia was represented by Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy, and Yana Lantratova, Russia's human rights commissioner. Ukraine sent Davyd Arakhamia, who leads Zelensky's Servant of the People faction in parliament, and Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian parliament's human rights commissioner, according to the White House and Meduza. Lantratova and Lubinets were the two officials who negotiated the Oleshky pause.

The White House said it was believed to be the first time a First Lady had personally brought together representatives of two nations at war for diplomacy. It said Mrs Trump acts as "Exclusive Intermediary", a role set out in written agreements Russia and Ukraine signed on 23 October.

"The ceasefire in Oleshky would not be possible without President Putin and President Zelensky," Mrs Trump said, according to the White House statement. "We have chosen humanity over war," she said, Newsweek reported. She did not take questions from reporters.

Dmitriev thanked her on Putin's behalf. "This humanitarian mission shows what can be achieved when compassion, determination and cooperation come together," he said, according to NBC News. Arakhamia said he hoped the arrangement would build momentum "to actually keep the peace when the peace comes", and the Ukrainian delegation asked for her humanitarian work to continue, Newsweek reported. Lubinets presented Mrs Trump with Ukraine's highest state award, the Order of Princess Olga, First Class.

## Background: the Oleshky pause

Oleshky sits on the left bank of the Dnipro river in Kherson region, opposite Kherson city, and has been held by Russian forces since early in the war. The local ceasefire began on 27 October and lasted six days. The White House says it allowed humanitarian aid in and "nearly 800 people" out; the figure has not been independently confirmed, and Meduza reported only that "several hundred" were evacuated.

The pause was not free of dispute. After it ended, Ukraine's General Staff said Russian troops had used it to rotate units and reinforce positions; Lubinets said monitors from both sides had found no violations. Russia has repeatedly rejected calls for a general ceasefire.

## The wider talks

The US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead Washington's negotiations. Peskov has said Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to Putin, will lead Russia's team in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky has described the coming round as a "team-level format" and called for a meeting of leaders to follow, according to NBC News.

The talks will be the first since President Donald Trump's Republicans lost both houses of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. The Kremlin said it "sincerely hoped" Trump would keep up his peace efforts after the vote, NBC News reported.

Moscow also hopes to hold a meeting of Putin, Trump and China's President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November. Beijing has said only that it is "in communication with relevant parties".

The fighting has not paused. Overnight into Thursday, Ukrainian drones set off fires at industrial sites in the Russian city of Ryazan, home to a large Rosneft oil refinery; the regional governor, Pavel Malkov, confirmed the fires but not damage to the refinery, the Kyiv Independent reported. On Tuesday Russia fired 289 drones and 76 missiles at Ukraine's energy system, according to Ukraine's air force, and Ukrainian officials say the death toll from Sunday's Russian strike on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha has risen to 43. Russia says it targets military and energy infrastructure. The figures from both sides cannot be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

India has called for dialogue and diplomacy throughout the war and has kept close ties with both Moscow and Kyiv. It is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil, so any settlement that changes Western sanctions on Russia would affect what India pays for fuel. The UAE, host of next week's talks, is one of India's closest partners in the Gulf.

The war also has a direct human cost for Indian families. The Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday that it continues to raise, "at various levels", the release of Indian nationals still serving with the Russian armed forces, including at External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting, The Tribune reported.

## What happens next

- 10-11 November: US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, led by Medinsky for Russia
- Letters from Mrs Trump to be delivered to Putin and Zelensky by Dmitriev and Arakhamia
- Lubinets and Lantratova have said they plan regular humanitarian missions to Oleshky
- 18-19 November: APEC summit in Shenzhen, where a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting is under discussion
